'''Cailee Spaeny''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|eɪ|l|i|_|ˈ|s|p|eɪ|n|i}} {{respell|KAY|lee|_|SPAY|nee}};<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 22, 2018 |title=Pacific Rim Uprising Cast Answer 50 of the Most Googled Kaiju Questions |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VF4txTaF7Fg |publisher=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] |website=[[YouTube]] |access-date=March 28, 2018 |archive-date=April 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210409043843/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VF4txTaF7Fg |url-status=live }}</ref> born July 24, 1998) is an American actress. Her first major roles were in the science fiction film ''[[Pacific Rim Uprising]]'' and the neo-noir film ''[[Bad Times at the El Royale]]'' (both 2018). Her television roles include appearances in the miniseries ''[[Devs (TV series)|Devs]]'' (2020), ''[[Mare of Easttown]]'' (2021), and the second season of the anthology series ''[[Beef (TV series)|Beef]]'' (2026). For producing the latter, she earned a nomination for the [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series]].

In 2023, Spaeny received critical acclaim for her portrayal of [[Priscilla Presley]] in the biographical film ''[[Priscilla (film)|Priscilla]]'', for which she received the [[Volpi Cup for Best Actress]] and a nomination for a [[Golden Globe Award]]. She gained further recognition for her roles in the dystopian drama film ''[[Civil War (film)|Civil War]]'' (2024), the science fiction horror film ''[[Alien: Romulus]]'' (2024), and the murder mystery ''[[Wake Up Dead Man]]'' (2025).

==Career==
===Early work (2018–2021)===
[[File:Cailee Spaeny, 2018 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Spaeny in 2018]]
Spaeny made her film debut in March 2018 in ''[[Pacific Rim: Uprising]]'', the sequel to ''[[Pacific Rim (film)|Pacific Rim]]'' (2013), directed by [[Steven S. DeKnight]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kroll |first=Justin |date=September 15, 2016 |title=Newcomer Cailee Spaeny Lands Female Lead in 'Pacific Rim 2' |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |url=https://variety.com/2016/film/news/cailee-spaeny-cast-in-pacific-rim-sequel-1201861762/ |access-date=November 22, 2017 |archive-date=September 18, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160918205604/http://variety.com/2016/film/news/cailee-spaeny-cast-in-pacific-rim-sequel-1201861762/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=White |first=James |date=September 15, 2016 |title=Pacific Rim sequel adds Cailee Spaeny |url=https://www.empireonline.com/people/scott-eastwood/pacific-rim-sequel-adds-cailee-spaeny/ |access-date=November 22, 2017 |magazine=Empire |archive-date=August 11, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180811134910/https://www.empireonline.com/people/scott-eastwood/pacific-rim-sequel-adds-cailee-spaeny/ |url-status=live }}</ref> She played Amara Namani, one of the protagonists,<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 15, 2016 |title=Cailee Spaeny Cast as Female Lead in Pacific Rim Sequel |work=[[ComingSoon.net]] |url=https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/766855-cailee-spaeny-cast-as-female-lead-in-pacific-rim-sequel |access-date=November 22, 2017 |archive-date=October 23, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231023070339/https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/766855-cailee-spaeny-cast-as-female-lead-in-pacific-rim-sequel |url-status=live }}</ref> an orphan who becomes a self‑taught engineer. Her performance was generally well-received, especially given that it was her first major film role.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2018/03/22/595179094/pacific-rim-uprising-serves-up-another-helping-of-mech-and-cheese|title='Pacific Rim Uprising' Serves Up Another Helping Of Mech And Cheese|date=March 22, 2018|access-date=November 26, 2016|publisher=[[National Public Radio]]|last=Weldon|first=Glen}}</ref>

Spaeny appeared in three more films in 2018. In September, she joined the cast of ''[[Bad Times at the El Royale]]'', a thriller directed by [[Drew Goddard]], in which she played Rose Summerspring, the younger sister of Emily Summerspring, played by [[Dakota Johnson]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Kit |first=Borys |date=September 15, 2016 |title=Drew Goddard's 'Bad Times at the El Royale' Adds Newcomer Cailee Spaeny |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/drew-goddards-bad-times-at-el-royale-adds-newcomer-cailee-spaeny-1032321 |access-date=November 22, 2017 |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |archive-date=March 10, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210310183148/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/drew-goddards-bad-times-at-el-royale-adds-newcomer-cailee-spaeny-1032321 |url-status=live }}</ref> The character is a fragile and impressionable teenager, manipulated by the cult led by Billy Lee, played by [[Chris Hemsworth]]. The role highlighted Spaeny's versatility; after playing the determined Amara in ''Pacific Rim: Uprising'', she took on a character marked by vulnerability.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thelist.com/1660287/cailee-spaeny-stunning-transformation/|title=The Stunning Transformation Of Cailee Spaeny|date=September 10, 2020|access-date=November 26, 2016|work=TheList.com|last=Langberg|first=Eric}}</ref>

In November, Spaeny appeared in ''[[On the Basis of Sex]]'', a biographical legal drama directed by [[Mimi Leder]] based on the life and early cases of [[Ruth Bader Ginsburg]], the second woman to serve as a justice of the [[Supreme Court of the United States]]. In the film, Spaeny played [[Jane C. Ginsburg]], the elder daughter of Ruth Bader Ginsburg, portrayed by [[Felicity Jones]].<ref name="Ginsburg">{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/features/how-felicity-jones-brought-punk-icon-ruth-bader-ginsburg-life-1172235|title=Making of 'On the Basis of Sex': How Felicity Jones Brought "Punk Icon" Ruth Bader Ginsburg to Life|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|last=Galuppo|first=Mia|date=January 7, 2019|access-date=February 17, 2026}}</ref><ref name="cailee"/> In December, she appeared in ''[[Vice (2018 film)|Vice]]'', a biographical comedy-drama written and directed by [[Adam McKay]] about the life of [[Dick Cheney]], played by [[Christian Bale]]. In the film, Spaeny played Lynne Vincent, a teenage version of [[Lynne Cheney]], with the adult version portrayed by [[Amy Adams]].<ref name="cailee"/>

In March 2020, Spaeny made her television debut in the miniseries ''[[Devs (TV series)|Devs]]'', created by [[Alex Garland]].<ref name="cailee"/> She played Lyndon, a central member of the team working on the secret Devs project developed by the technology company Amaya.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://collider.com/devs-interview-cailee-spaeny-lyndon-gender/|title=Devs: Cailee Spaeny on Why She Plays a Male Character on the Show|date=April 9, 2020|access-date=November 26, 2016|work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|last=Radish|first=Christina}}</ref> In October, she starred in ''[[The Craft: Legacy]]'', a supernatural horror film written and directed by [[Zoe Lister-Jones]], conceived as a sequel to ''[[The Craft (film)|The Craft]]'' (1996).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Galuppo |first=Mia |date=June 21, 2019 |title='The Craft' Reboot Finds Lead With Cailee Spaeny (Exclusive) |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/craft-cailee-spaeny-lead-reboot-1220281 |access-date=October 8, 2019 |work=The Hollywood Reporter |archive-date=January 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113215122/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/craft-cailee-spaeny-lead-reboot-1220281 |url-status=live }}</ref> This was Spaeny's first leading role in a film, as well as her first time going through a casting process. The film follows a group of young women who develop supernatural abilities.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/why-the-craft-legacy-was-the-missing-piece-for-cailee-spaeny-4081995/|title=Why 'The Craft: Legacy' was the "Missing Piece" for Cailee Spaeny|date=November 23, 2020|access-date=November 26, 2016|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|last=Davids|first=Brian}}</ref>

In January 2021, Spaeny appeared in ''[[How It Ends (2021 film)|How It Ends]]'', an independent apocalyptic comedy also directed by Lister-Jones. She played Young Liza (also called "Little Liza" or "Younger Self"), a teenage version of the protagonist Liza, played as an adult by the director.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2020/film/news/sundance-film-festival-announces-2021-lineup-1234854059/|title=Sundance Film Festival Lineup Features 38 First-Time Directors, Including Rebecca Hall and Robin Wright|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|first=Peter|last=Debruge|date=December 15, 2020|access-date=December 15, 2020}}</ref> In April, she joined the cast of the [[HBO]] miniseries ''[[Mare of Easttown]]'', created by [[Brad Ingelsby]] and starring [[Kate Winslet]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Romano |first=Nick |date=February 17, 2021 |title=Kate Winslet gets her prestige murder mystery drama in HBO's Mare of Easttown trailer |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |url=https://ew.com/tv/mare-of-easttown-trailer-kate-winslet/ |access-date=February 19, 2021 |archive-date=March 18, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210318100442/https://ew.com/tv/mare-of-easttown-trailer-kate-winslet/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Spaeny played Erin McMenamin, a 17-year-old single mother living in Easttown, a small working‑class town in [[Pennsylvania]]. Her character faces financial difficulties while caring for her son, who needs an expensive hearing surgery.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://collider.com/cailee-spaeny-mare-of-easttown-hbo/|title=Kate Winslet Solves Cailee Spaeny's Murder in This Twisty HBO Miniseries|date=August 25, 2024|access-date=November 26, 2016|work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|last=Haines|first=Samuel Wyatt}}</ref>

===Breakthrough (2022–present)===
In April 2022, Spaeny joined the cast of the series ''[[The First Lady (American TV series)|The First Lady]]'', which depicts the personal and family lives of three [[First Ladies of the United States]]: [[Eleanor Roosevelt]], [[Betty Ford]], and [[Michelle Obama]]. Spaeny played [[Anna Roosevelt Halsted|Anna Eleanor Roosevelt]] (also known as Anna Roosevelt Halsted), the only daughter of [[Franklin D. Roosevelt]] and [[Eleanor Roosevelt]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2021/07/the-first-lady-ellen-burstyn-eliza-scanlen-cailee-spaeny-recur-showtime-anthology-series-1234798988/|title='The First Lady': Ellen Burstyn, Eliza Scanlen, Cailee Spaeny To Recur On Showtime Anthology Series|website=Deadline Hollywood|first=Denise|last=Petski|date=July 23, 2021|access-date=July 27, 2021|archive-date=July 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210723181550/https://deadline.com/2021/07/the-first-lady-ellen-burstyn-eliza-scanlen-cailee-spaeny-recur-showtime-anthology-series-1234798988/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="cailee">{{cite web|url=https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/entretenimento/quem-e-cailee-spaeny-atriz-que-estrela-guerra-civil-ao-lado-de-wagner-moura/ |title=Quem é Cailee Spaeny, atriz que estrela "Guerra Civil" ao lado de Wagner Moura |date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=February 17, 2026 |publisher=[[CNN Brasil]] |author=Marina Toledo|language=pt}}</ref>

[[File:Cailee Spaeny 2023 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|right|Spaeny at the [[2023 BFI London Film Festival]]]]
In September, Spaeny was cast as [[Priscilla Beaulieu Presley]] in the film ''[[Priscilla (film)|Priscilla]]'', directed by [[Sofia Coppola]], alongside [[Jacob Elordi]] as [[Elvis Presley]]. Based on Priscilla Presley's 1985 memoir ''[[Elvis and Me]]'',<ref name="Priscilla">{{cite web|last=Jackson|first=Angelique|url=https://variety.com/2022/film/news/jacob-elordi-elvis-cailee-spaeny-priscilla-presley-sofia-coppola-1235369454/|title=Jacob Elordi to Play Elvis, Cailee Spaeny Is Priscilla Presley in Sofia Coppola's Film 'Priscilla'|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=September 12, 2022|access-date=October 6, 2022}}</ref> the film premiered at the [[80th Venice International Film Festival]]. Spaeny was widely acclaimed for her performance, which earned her the [[Volpi Cup for Best Actress]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2023/09/venice-film-festival-2023-awards-winners-full-list-1235541624/|title=Venice Winners: Golden Lion Goes To Yorgos Lanthimos For 'Poor Things'; Hamaguchi, Sarsgaard, Spaeny Also Score — Full List|website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]]|first1=Nancy|last1=Tartaglione|first2=Zac|last2=Ntim|date=9 September 2023|access-date=9 September 2023|archive-date=September 10, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230910044037/https://deadline.com/2023/09/venice-film-festival-2023-awards-winners-full-list-1235541624/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://thefashionenthusiast.uk/stories/cailee-spaeny-brings-florals-to-the-2024-golden-globes-red-carpet|title=Cailee Spaeny Brings Florals to the 2024 Golden Globes Red Carpet|website=The Fashion Enthusiast|date=7 January 2024|access-date=8 January 2024|archive-date=January 8, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240108081748/https://thefashionenthusiast.uk/stories/cailee-spaeny-brings-florals-to-the-2024-golden-globes-red-carpet|url-status=live}}</ref> At the premiere, she watched the film alongside Priscilla Presley herself, who was moved by the work and by Spaeny's performance.<ref name="Priscillap">{{cite web|url=https://people.com/cailee-spaeny-talks-watching-priscilla-with-priscilla-presley-7966065|title='Priscilla' Star Cailee Spaeny Says Watching Movie with Priscilla Presley in Venice Was 'Absolutely Surreal'|date=September 6, 2023|access-date=February 18, 2026|work=[[People (magazine)|People]]}}</ref> Of her preparation for playing the character, Spaeny said: "It was very daunting, but I was very lucky to spend some time with Priscilla, and she was very generous. When you're playing someone so well-known, that support makes all the difference. She was very kind to me and supported me, and that was my main source, besides the book."<ref name="Priscillap"/>

In 2024, Spaeny starred in the dystopian war drama and action film ''[[Civil War (film)|Civil War]]'', directed by [[Alex Garland]], with whom she had worked on ''Devs''. She played Jessie Collin, an aspiring [[war photographer]].<ref name="cailee"/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Grobar |first1=Matt |title=Alex Garland Reteams With A24 For Action Epic ''Civil War''; Kirsten Dunst, Wagner Moura & More Set To Star |url=https://deadline.com/2022/01/civil-war-kirsten-dunst-more-to-star-in-alex-garland-a24-film-1234917411/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=21 January 2022 |date=January 21, 2022 |archive-date=April 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220418080027/https://deadline.com/2022/01/civil-war-kirsten-dunst-more-to-star-in-alex-garland-a24-film-1234917411/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Also in 2024, she starred in ''[[Alien: Romulus]]'', a film directed by [[Fede Álvarez]] and produced by [[Ridley Scott]], part of the [[Alien (franchise)|''Alien'' franchise]]. She played the [[space colonist]] Rain Carradine.<ref name="alien">{{cite web|title=Fede Álvarez's ''Alien'' Movie Rounds Out Cast (Exclusive)|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/fede-alvarez-alien-movie-cast-1235340396/|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=March 3, 2023|access-date=July 17, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Kroll |first1=Justin |title=Cailee Spaeny Circling New ''Alien'' Movie At 20th Century Fox And Scott Free |url=https://deadline.com/2022/11/cailee-spaeny-alien-movie-20th-century-scott-free-1235174184/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=November 16, 2022 |access-date=November 16, 2022 |archive-date=November 16, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116194746/https://deadline.com/2022/11/cailee-spaeny-alien-movie-20th-century-scott-free-1235174184/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Jordan Hoffman]] of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' called Spaeny "the finest weapon in the arsenal...  differentiating herself quite a bit from the doe-eyed characters she played in ''Civil War'' and ''Priscilla''."<ref>{{Cite web |title='Alien: Romulus' launches Cailee Spaeny into winning gross-out orbit |url=https://ew.com/alien-romulus-review-cailee-spaeny-launches-winning-gross-out-orbit-8694798 |access-date=2024-08-17 |website=EW.com }}</ref>

In 2025, Spaeny appeared in ''[[Wake Up Dead Man]]'', a film in the ''[[Knives Out (film series)|Knives Out]]'' franchise, written and directed by [[Rian Johnson]] and starring [[Daniel Craig]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kroll |first1=Justin |title=Josh O'Connor And Cailee Spaeny Join Daniel Craig In ''Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery'' |url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/josh-oconnor-cailee-spaeny-daniel-craig-wake-up-dead-man-a-knives-out-mystery-1235942121/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=May 28, 2024 |date=May 27, 2024 |archive-date=May 28, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240528202442/https://deadline.com/2024/05/josh-oconnor-cailee-spaeny-daniel-craig-wake-up-dead-man-a-knives-out-mystery-1235942121/ |url-status=live }}</ref> She played Simone Vivane, a former cellist of international renown whose career was interrupted by chronic [[neuropathic pain]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/wake-up-dead-man-cast-guide|title=Meet the Cast of Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery|date=December 17, 2025|access-date=November 27, 2016|publisher=Tudum by [[Netflix]]|last=McIlvane|first=Brookie}}</ref>

In 2026, Spaeny starred in the second season of the anthology series ''[[Beef (TV series)|Beef]]'', alongside [[Oscar Isaac]], [[Carey Mulligan]], and [[Charles Melton]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Petski|first=Denise|title='Beef' Confirms Season 2 With Oscar Isaac, Carey Mulligan, Charles Melton & Cailee Spaeny|url=https://deadline.com/2024/10/beef-season-2-cast-oscar-isaac-carey-mulligan-charles-melton-cailee-spaeny-1236145408/ |website=Deadline|access-date=October 22, 2024|date=October 22, 2024}}</ref><ref name="beef">{{cite web|url=https://rollingstone.com.br/entretenimento/tudo-o-que-sabemos-sobre-a-2a-temporada-da-serie-treta/|title=Tudo o que sabemos sobre a 2ª temporada da série 'Treta'|date=January 7, 2026|access-date=February 17, 2026|work=[[Rolling Stone]]|last=Cardoso|first=Giulia|language=pt}}</ref> She was also cast in ''[[Elden Ring (film)|Elden Ring]]'', a live-action film adaptation of the eponymous game<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/elden-ring-movie-cast-1236569064/|title='Elden Ring' Live-Action Movie Adds Tom Burke, Havana Rose Liu, Sonoya Mizuno, Emma Laird as Production Begins|date=April 20, 2026|access-date=April 20, 2026|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|last=Kit|first=Borys}}</ref> set for a March 2028 release.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2026/04/alex-garland-elden-ring-march-2028-cailee-spaeny-1236865471/|title=Alex Garland's 'Elden Ring' Adaptation At A24 Sets A March 2028 Release In Imax; Cailee Spaeny Among New Additions To Cast|date=April 20, 2026|access-date=April 20, 2026|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|last=Kroll|first=Justin}}</ref>

extract:
Cailee Spaeny ( KAY-lee SPAY-nee; born July 24, 1998) is an American actress. Her first major roles were in the science fiction film Pacific Rim Uprising and the neo-noir film Bad Times at the El Royale (both 2018). Her television roles include appearances in the miniseries Devs (2020), Mare of Easttown (2021), and the second season of the anthology series Beef (2026). For producing the latter, she earned a nomination for the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series.
In 2023, Spaeny received critical acclaim for her portrayal of Priscilla Presley in the biographical film Priscilla, for which she received the Volpi Cup for Best Actress and a nomination for a Golden Globe Award. She gained further recognition for her roles in the dystopian drama film Civil War (2024), the science fiction horror film Alien: Romulus (2024), and the murder mystery Wake Up Dead Man (2025).
